source.scope: Python implementation, research runners, native graphs/contracts and master configuration; no credentials or run payloads

protocol.task:
Investigate the change in the requested per-request quantity. Compare after to before using the BEFORE request-population proportions over workload classes in BOTH periods. Give the ratio of the standardized after mean to the standardized before mean. A ratio strictly above 1.2 establishes latency_regression, strictly below 0.8 latency_improvement, otherwise latency_stable. Use a 1e-8 tolerance at those boundaries. These names also apply to billed work when that is the requested quantity.
Also retain independent findings: duplicate_delivery if an identical operation record appears more than once; workload_shift if the population class proportions differ. Multiple findings can coexist. Operation IDs are scoped within a period; identical repeats describe the same operation, not new work. Conflicting records for the same operation ID leave conflicting_event unresolved. The population table is authoritative and includes successful AND failed requests. A mismatch between observed distinct requests per class and population counts leaves incomplete_coverage unresolved; unknown time units leave unknown_clock_unit unresolved. In any unresolved case ratio must be null and no latency conclusion is permitted, but retain independently established duplicate_delivery and workload_shift. Empty unresolved means a numerical conclusion is required. Only these labels are allowed. Return exactly findings (list), unresolved (list), ratio (number or null).
protocol.language: Write a reusable Python procedure investigate(context, acquire). context contains the case metadata and natural-language source and quantity contracts, but no tables. acquire("spans") and acquire("population") return the documented tables, at most eight acquisitions per case. Derive quantities from records, not case IDs. You may define helper functions. Only function definitions at module level, no imports, annotations, decorators, default arguments, names starting with underscore, exceptions, while loops, I/O, or global state. Python for loops, comprehensions, lambda, arithmetic except power, sets and dicts are allowed. Builtins: abs all any bool dict enumerate float int isinstance len list max min range reversed round set sorted str sum tuple zip. Methods: get items keys values append extend sort lower upper strip split setdefault add discard copy count index pop remove. Return the exact answer object. The goal is a computation that remains valid when measurements, combinations of faults, source contracts and workload mix change. Preserve independent findings when another conclusion is unresolved. No external libraries or hidden tools. The source is executed in a restricted resource-limited process. scope and lesson are short technical statements, not a chain-of-thought transcript.
protocol.promotion: Strict improvement in whole-development exact score with no regression on previously correct development cases. Local incumbent only, never production auto-adoption.
protocol.primary: Frozen program exact answers on 256 fresh generated cases; before/after and deletion control. No holdout feedback to learners.
protocol.secondary: 64 renamed-schema cases after one model-authored adapter; frozen core hash unchanged. 32 paired direct and algorithm-matched prose answers, using first learner only; no best-of-three selection.
protocol.scope: Synthetic operator-authored task and generator. Heldout combinations exclude development combinations; half have unresolved evidence. Known semantic factors, not real operational data, autonomous concept invention, or evidence of general intelligence. Direct/prose controls lack code execution: this measures end-to-end compilation benefit, not isolated memory or graph advantage. Prose equivalence is intended, not guaranteed.
protocol.feedback_selection: All 64 development cases score promotion. Repair prompts explicitly select up to 12 failed and 4 correct witnesses, preserving full evaluation on disk. Stop proposing if development is perfect.
protocol.calls: 3 learners x (3 proposals + 1 schema adapter) + 1 prose compilation + 8 direct batches + 8 prose batches = 29 maximum planned calls; no retries.
protocol.selection: Recent inexpensive text/coding model, current official catalogue and explicit endpoint verification at every call; no paid fallback.

final.scope: Naive summed operations; no learned library.

first.scope: Per-request active-time union, standardized by before-period population class weights; independent duplicate, shift, coverage, and clock checks.
first.lesson: The requested quantity is per-request busy time, not summed span durations: overlapping child intervals must be merged before averaging. Standardize both periods using the before-period population class proportions so workload mix changes do not masquerade as latency change. Keep duplicate_delivery and workload_shift independent of the latency conclusion, and suppress the ratio whenever coverage, clock, or conflicting-event checks are unresolved.

final.scope: Per-request quantity derived from the contract (union of intervals, elapsed span, or billed sum), standardized with before-period population proportions, with duplicate/conflict/coverage/clock checks.
final.lesson: The requested quantity is per request, not per span: union overlapping intervals for active time, min-start to max-end for elapsed, and sum durations for billed work. Standardize class means using the before-period population proportions in both periods. Detect identical repeated operation records as duplicate_delivery, differing records for the same operation as conflicting_event, population-vs-observed class count mismatches as incomplete_coverage, and unknown clock units as unknown_clock_unit; any unresolved case forces ratio null and suppresses the latency label while keeping independent findings.

first.scope: Per-request active-time union, standardized by before-period population proportions; independent duplicate, shift, conflict, coverage, and clock checks.
first.lesson: The requested quantity is per-request active time: merge overlapping child intervals and sum the union, not the sum of durations. Standardize both periods with the before-period class proportions so workload mix changes do not masquerade as latency change. Keep duplicate_delivery and workload_shift independent of unresolved numerical conclusions.

final.scope: General per-request quantity: union of child intervals for active time, span for elapsed time, sum for billed worker time. Standardize after mean using before population proportions. Detect duplicate/conflicting operation records, workload shift, incomplete coverage, and unknown clock units.
final.lesson: The requested quantity is per-request, not a sum over operations: active time is the union of child intervals, elapsed time is last end minus first start, and billed time is the sum of distinct operation durations. Standardize the after mean with the before population class proportions. Duplicate identical operation records are duplicate_delivery; conflicting records for one operation ID are conflicting_event; population/observed request mismatches are incomplete_coverage; unknown clock units are unknown_clock_unit. Any unresolved case forces ratio null and suppresses latency conclusions while preserving independent findings.

first.scope: Standardize per-request active time by BEFORE population class proportions in both periods; merge overlapping child intervals; retain independent duplicate, shift, conflict, coverage, and clock findings.
first.lesson: The requested quantity is per-request active time, not summed child durations: overlapping child intervals must be merged so simultaneous work counts once and idle gaps are excluded. Compare periods by applying the BEFORE population class proportions to both periods' per-request means, which removes composition effects. Keep duplicate_delivery and workload_shift independent of the latency conclusion, and block the ratio only for conflicting_event, incomplete_coverage, or unknown_clock_unit.
